notes.1a: (i) Many candidates correctly stated plants or fungi but many incorrectly stated mammals or other animal groups.
notes.1aii: Wings was the most common correct answer. Antennae was a common incorrect answer.
notes.1iii: This question proved to be demanding and few correctly completed the table.
notes.1b: (i) Few candidates gained two marks on this question. Many gave live or adapt, rather than the appropriate scientific terms.
notes.1bii: Generally, candidates answered this question well although some wrote about colour despite only having a black and white image.
notes.2a: (i) This question was generally well answered. Protein synthesis was the most challenging function for candidates.
notes.2aii: Again, generally well answered. The most common mistake was to identify E (nucleus) as being present in a bacterial cell.
notes.2b: Most candidates answered this correctly although some incorrectly stated death.
notes.3a: Many candidates mentioned enzymes but did not explain their function further than breaking down food. Very few referred to molecules or solubility.
notes.3b: (i) The majority of candidates gave carbohydrate rather than starch as the substrate for amylase. Very few gained two marks for the products of the breakdown of fat; most stated fatty acids only. The mark most awarded was for amino acids.
notes.3bii: There were several alternative answers to this question as many enzymes are produced in multiple sites. Some candidates named structures that were unrelated to digestion e.g. muscles.
notes.3c: (i) Few candidates were awarded this mark. Most incorrectly wrote either gastric acid, stomach acid, lactic acid, or amino acid.
notes.3cii: Many candidates gained the microorganism mark, but few were able to recall that the acid provided an optimum pH for enzymes.
notes.4a: The first part of this question was well answered, although some gave arteries and veins the wrong way round. Few candidates correctly named capillaries and valves.
notes.4b: (i) Most candidates correctly counted the six heartbeats.
notes.4bii: Some candidates found the calculation demanding. Common incorrect calculations were. 6/4 = 150% or 4/6 = 66%.
notes.4c: This was generally well answered. Some put healthy diet rather than balanced diet or any details of what either of these meant. Many candidates mentioned stress and smoking. Some mentioned drinking unqualified, rather than drinking alcohol.
notes.4d: Few candidates were awarded this mark. Many described how sound is transmitted through a stethoscope.
notes.5a: (i) Most candidates correctly stated aerobic respiration. The most common incorrect answer was cellular.
notes.5aii: Many candidates found it difficult to interpret this diagram. Some candidates gave oxygen and carbon dioxide even though these were given in the question. Some gave glucose and water the wrong way round.
notes.5iii: Many candidates correctly stated diffusion although several stated respiration.
notes.5b: Generally, well answered although many incorrectly stated photosynthesis. Some candidates gave three different examples of muscle contraction.
notes.5c: Very few candidates were awarded all three marks for this question. Almost all candidates wrote about volume of gas rather than the rate of respiration.
notes.6a: Most candidates gained two or three marks on this question but many stated that the seed also needs light and nutrients from the soil.
notes.6b: (i) Many candidates found it difficult to apply their knowledge to the diagram. Some drew the root and shoot growing horizontally and several ignored the root and shoot partly drawn on the diagram and drew their own coming directly from the seed.
notes.6bii: Tropism was not well known by most candidates.
notes.7a: This question was generally well answered. Many candidates did not identify the site of production of testosterone correctly, stating E rather that C. Some candidates wrote the name of the structure instead of the letter, this was accepted.
notes.7b: Most candidates correctly named oestrogen although some gave progesterone or testosterone.
notes.7c: Generally, well answered although many candidates put ovule rather than egg or ovum and fecundation for fertilisation.
notes.8a: Many candidates could not name a source of methane gas.
notes.8b: The first two gaps were well answered. The last gap was less well-known, with several candidates making errors reading the values from the graph.
notes.8c: (i) Generally well answered although several candidates put factories.
notes.8cii: Few candidates scored well here. A common error was to state greenhouse effect instead of enhanced greenhouse effect.
notes.8d: (i) There were many incorrect answers to this question with few naming anaerobic respiration or fermentation.
notes.8dii: Most candidates were awarded some marks for describing the disadvantages of monocultures. Some described the problems associated with burning biofuels rather than growing them.
notes.key_messages:
Candidates would benefit from reading questions carefully, as they often contain specific information that must
be used in the answer. For example, when the question asks for five lines to be drawn, it is important that only
five lines are drawn. Also, the question may ask for a definition rather than a discussion and that indicates the
level of detail required in the answer.
notes.general_comments:
Many candidates were well prepared for the exam and had obviously referred to past papers and mark
schemes when preparing. This type of preparation allows candidates to express themselves clearly.
Command words such as ‘describe’, ‘explain’, ‘suggest’ and ‘compare’ require different responses from
candidates. If a description is required, including a reference to a graph or table, then it will be expected that
data will be used in the description given. Many candidates can do this effectively. An explanation requires
more than just a description and candidates should be encouraged to practise the difference between ‘explain’
and ‘describe’. Correct spelling of certain words is expected e.g., uterus, ureter, and urethra.
